article_text:
Films and events

Galas

Fatherland

In a masterclass of control and precision, Paweł Pawlikowski explores the fragmented soul of postwar Germany through a father-daughter road trip dominated by personal ghosts.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Screening at cinemas around the UK – find out more .

Credits

Director Paweł Pawlikowski

Screenwriters Paweł Pawlikowski, Henk Handloegten

With Sandra Hüller, Hanns Zischler, August Diehl

Poland-Germany-Italy-France 2026. 82min

Courtesy of MUBI

Languages German, English, French, Russian With English subtitles

Access information

Wednesday 14 October 18:15

Audio description

Closed Captions (CC) via WatchWord smart glasses

Thursday 15 October 15:30

Audio description

Descriptive subtitles

Sunday 18 October 13:20

Audio description

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

In 1949, Erika (a superb Sandra Hüller) is accompanying her father, Nobel laureate author Thomas Mann, on a literary tour through West and East Germany. As family tragedy strikes, it becomes apparent that the spiritual healing Mann deems essential for the divided country may be necessary for their own relationship. It’s an impeccably shot and evocative drama that meditates on the healing process for a fractured national identity.

Diana Cipriano

Content advice

Contains scenes of suicide.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

A Man of His Time

The banality of evil is brilliantly exposed in this thought-provoking and singular portrait of a mediocre yet ambitious bureaucrat in Nazi-occupied France.

Coward

Lukas Dhont’s latest gem is a luminous and deeply romantic love story, set against the backdrop of the First World War.

Woman Unknown

In May el-Toukhy’s powerful third feature, Marie, a survivor with secrets, navigates retribution and the febrile chaos of life in post-war Denmark.

article_text:
In 1987, agnès b. travelled to Moscow, then the capital of the Soviet Union, for five days, accompanied by Philippe Trétiack, journalist and writer for ELLE magazine. Her mission: to discover new fashions, new styles and new tastes, in a country and among a population about which she then knew almost nothing.

On arrival, she found herself plunged into a world far removed from her Western points of reference: silent crowds, immense spaces, a difficult daily life, and clothes that were often dark and plain. But over the course of those five days, her gaze shifted. Armed with her film Nikon, agnès b. began to photograph, for herself, what she discovered as she moved around Moscow. Children huddled against their parents, shopkeepers in astonishing outfits, passers-by, faces, attitudes, clothes: so many details that caught her attention and fed her pleasure in discovery.

In black and white as well as in colour, these photographs were thus born almost spontaneously, alongside the report she was producing for ELLE. They testify less to a desire to document the Soviet Union than to the curious, attentive eye that agnès b. turns on people and on everything around her.

Through these candid images emerges the Moscow of 1987, only a few years before the disappearance of the Soviet Union: a city and an era captured through a multitude of ordinary scenes, encounters and details that surprised, amused or moved agnès b. during those five days.

article_text:
Feature

Jazmine Hayes Charts Community Displacement, Resilience in Brownsville Art Commission

“I genuinely want any child that walks through this door to be and feel protected,” the East New York-raised artist told Hyperallergic.

I Am Protected (2026) for the Brownsville Multi-Service Center (all photos Azikiwe Aboagye unless otherwise noted)

Last month, three New York City agencies unveiled a new $128 million multi-service center in Brooklyn's Brownsville neighborhood, featuring an extensive public art commission by local artist and community educator Jazmine Hayes.

Through the Department of Cultural Affairs' (DCLA) Percent for Art program, Hayes's four-part commission, I Am Protected (2026), graces each entryway to the building with symbolically empowering designs that channel the cultural history of Brownsville's residents and carve out space for youth ambition and curiosity.

“I genuinely want any child that walks through this door to be and feel protected,” Hayes said in an interview with Hyperallergic. “ I want them to have affirmations of care, support, and community.”

Born and raised in the adjacent neighborhood of East New York, Hayes knew Brownsville well and was excited at the opportunity when DCLA reached out, especially after completing another public artwork nearby for the New York City Housing Authority's (NYCHA) Brownsville Houses the year before.

Editor’s note: T his story contains details of alleged sexual offenses that some readers may find distressing .

Russell Brand has claimed that “consent is more important than sex itself” as he forcefully denied the rape charges against him during a trial in London.

Taking to the witness stand at Southwark Crown Court on Wednesday morning, the Forgetting Sarah Marshall star said his “entire life has been consumed by these allegations” since UK press reports about his conduct in 2023. Brand said he had “devoted” himself to attempting to get to the bottom of the accusations.

Related Stories

Russell Brand Indecent Assault Charge Reduced By Judge; Trial Continues

Russell Brand's Former Assistant Claims Women Came To Comedian's Flat For Sex All The Time But He "Never Seemed Happy" Afterwards

Wearing an open white shirt and blazer, Brand was called forward to the dock, said his name and forcefully denied all charges put to him by his barrister Ian Winter. He replied “no” to each charge loudly as he was asked. He said no one was willing to give evidence on his behalf. Deadline has been reporting daily from a live video feed of the courtroom since the trial began.

Watch on Deadline

Standing up and facing the jury as he gave evidence, Brand told the court: “Consent is fundamental, essential, necessary, and in many ways more important than the sex itself.”

Brand On Alleged 1999 Rape

Brand was asked about Complainant 1 (C1) , who alleged that she was raped by the comedian after meeting him on the fringes of the Labour Party Conference in Bournemouth in 1999. The woman was in her twenties at the time of the alleged incident. She, along with the other five complainants, has a lifelong right to anonymity.

After attending a cabaret event in which Brand was performing, the pair returned to C1’s hotel room. “I hoped there was at least the possibility of sex,” Brand told the jury. Brand said he was attracted to C1: “She was vivacious, vital, loquacious, unusual.”

C1 claimed Brand pushed her on the bed, pulled down her trousers and underwear, and proceeded to rape her. The woman repeatedly told police that she remembered his weight on her and that he attempted to put his fingers in her mouth. C1 alleged that he was “pushing and pushing” until he ejaculated. “I know I said, ‘No,’” she told police.

Brand told a different story. He remembered “fooling around” and then having “sex with a condom.” Brand claimed that he spoke to C1 during intercourse, asking her “all the things that elicit approval,” including if she was enjoying the encounter. Brand said it “wasn’t a familiar situation” for himself because he could not recall being with an older woman before.

Brand Says Alleged Anal Rape Victim Was “Coquettish”

Winter turned to Complainant 5 (C5), who alleged that she was anally raped by Brand in 2009 at his home in Hampstead, north London, after first meeting him backstage at a Hammersmith Apollo stand-up gig.

C5 admitted having a consensual sexual encounter with Brand and another woman in his dressing room after the Hammersmith Apollo gig, during which she gave the comedian oral sex. Brand said he recalled the encounter in “startling detail” because C5 “put her tongue in my anus.”

They met days later at his home in Hampstead. Both accept they had consensual vaginal sex with a condom. C5 then accused Brand of anally raping her. C5 alleged Brand said to her, “I want you to feel my cum,” at which point he ejaculated inside her anus and she realized he had removed his condom. Multiple witnesses recalled C5 being in physical pain and “extremely distressed” after the incident.

Brand admitted “talking dirty” to C5 and saying words to the effect of, “I wanna cum in you, I wanna cum in your ass.” He recalled C5 being “coquettish” and that she consented to anal sex. Brand said he took steps to lubricate C5 because anal sex would have been “painful” otherwise. “She consented to continuing sexual activity without a condom,” Brand said.

The Despicable Me actor told the court that he saved C5’s number in his phone with the initial “T,” which he said was an abbreviation for “tart,” and “AP,” meaning “anal play.” The number also included “**,” which Brand said meant: “Never forget this individual — this was a memorable encounter.” Riel Karmy-Jones, the prosecution barrister, accused Brand of retrofitting his definitions to fit his evidence. Karmy-Jones alleged that “AP” could just as easily stand for “after party.”

Brand Denies Alleged 2004 Oral Rape

Brand faced questions on Complainant C3 (C3), who alleges he orally raped her in the toilet of a London bar at the birthday party of a TV producer. The court heard a police interview from C3 last week alleging Brand “literally just grabbed my boobs” and dragged her into the toilet before forcing his penis into her mouth and subsequently ejaculating.

According to Brand today, he initially had no recollection of encountering C3 before he returned to the bar with his solicitors after the allegation was put to him and meeting C3 came back to him.

However, Brand firmly denied the allegation, saying he arrived at the party and was told by the TV producer, “There’s a bird here who really wants to meet you mate.”

He described C3 as being “wide eyed, enthusiastic and flirty” and denied grabbing her breast, but instead said they both decided to go to the toilet cubicle together.

After some “kissing, touching and fooling around” and while it’s “possible” he “would have taken my penis out of my trousers,” Brand said “the environment was unsuitable for me to meet the goal I went in there with,” which would have been achieving an orgasm.

He said he left the bar with C3 and went to a different London bar, at which point they lost each other and he “met some attractive women specifically from a TV channel called Babestation.”

Barred From Visiting Son In Hospital

After the Channel 4 documentary about the allegations was aired in 2023, Brand told the court he was not allowed to visit his son, who was receiving open-heart surgery in a London hospital.

Brand claimed he was told, “due to the material that had been published in the public eye, they had to bar my attendance and presence.” “They were unclear about what particular reason there was, but that was the reason they gave to my wife Laura and I,” he told the court. Brand’s wife Laura Gallagher attended court.

Brand said he did not call Channel 4’s Russell Brand: In Plain Sight a “documentary.” Pointedly, he said, “I call it a TV show,” when answering questions from his barrister.

Brand faces three charges of rape, three counts of sexual assault and now one of attempted indecent assault, reduced from indecent assault, based on allegations made by six women . His team has today started setting out its defense.

The prosecution wrapped this morning with a final piece of evidence concerning a conversation between one of the complainants and a journalist for The Sunday Times, which broke news of the Brand allegations alongside Channel 4.

On Tuesday, a pre-prepared statement that Brand made to police when he was interviewed between 2023 and 2025 was read to the court in which Brand said he “had sexual encounters in countless locations and scenarios, often with people I had just met,” but firmly denied ever having non-consensual sex.

The trial continues.

article_text:
Marshall To: Blank Notes

From ‘Blank Notes’ by Marshall To, published by Charcoal Press

Marshall To grew up hearing stories about the supernatural world, one that co-existed with the physical world. His family, Chinese immigrants in rural Canada, was Taoist. They believed that humans were surrounded by the spirits of loved ones. He remembers celebrating the Hungry Ghosts Festival on the 15th day of the seventh month in the lunar calendar, when the gates of Hell were opened to allow ghosts to roam the earth in search of food. He explains that the festival is a time to celebrate and venerate deceased loved ones. But it also is a dangerous time because the ghosts are hungry. To get what they want, the spirits can take many forms – birds, snakes, foxes, tigers and even a beautiful man or woman.

From ‘Blank Notes’ by Marshall To, published by Charcoal Press

When he was younger, To was embarrassed by these festivals and rituals that clashed with the small town rural Canadian culture he was surrounded by. But after spending time exploring these rituals and family memories, he has embraced them and in the process has created a book that is mesmerizing and unique.

From ‘Blank Notes’ by Marshall To, published by Charcoal Press

Most of his photographs were taken at night and he is intensely afraid of the dark. That tension and fear is reflected in his photographs – a mix of animals, rituals like burning incense, forlorn landscapes and people who often look like they are in a dream. The black matte paper used throughout the book, the grainy photos, the glare of the flashlight illuminating some photos, all add to a feeling of anxiety that pulls you into To’s spectacular ghost story.

An interview with the artist follows.

From ‘Blank Notes’ by Marshall To, published by Charcoal Press

Marshall To is a multidisciplinary artist focusing on photography, painting and illustrations. He grew up in a Taoist family in a small town called Red Deer which created a unique integration of western landscape and eastern beliefs. He moved to Vancouver where he currently resides, working as a Chef. Growing up in a Chinese immigrant household, food was integral to the culture and more importantly was a language used to communicate. Unsatisfied with just cooking, Marshall began taking pictures of food and quickly began photographing and styling for local magazines and websites, and then endeavored to seek even more with photography and art.

Website: https://marshalljamesto.com/ Instagram: @ marshalljamesto @c harcoalpress Link to order “Blank Notes” from Charcoal Press

From ‘Blank Notes’ by Marshall To, published by Charcoal Press

Artist Statement: “I remember having a fever one night after visiting my grandmother’s grave. I Felt like I was on fire, twisted inside out. I could smell the incense and heard frantic prayers. I was helpless, and felt controlled by something else…something other. The prayers repeated over and over as the fever and incense burned. All of a sudden, a deafening CRACK sounded from inside the ceiling. It was loud as thunder, and then there was silence. The incense burnt out and the prayers stopped. It seemed only natural that the veil separating the living and the dead might be as thin as the line between life and death.”

From ‘Blank Notes’ by Marshall To, published by Charcoal Press

Congratulations. Remarkable book. Unlike anything I’ve seen. What does the title, “Blank Notes,” mean?

Thank you very much. It’s been a long time coming, and I’m very proud of what we’ve been able to accomplish.

In Taoist culture during funerals, festivals or any days of remembrance, we burn blank paper notes that are supposed to resemble money so that those who have passed can use it to spend there. I remember how fun it was as a child throwing this fake money up in the air or putting it into a metal bucket to burn and it stuck with me.

From ‘Blank Notes’ by Marshall To, published by Charcoal Press

Your father, a Taoist, believed that humans were surrounded by the spirits of loved ones, that the supernatural and physical worlds coexisted. You must have heard a lot of ghost stories from your dad growing up. You mention the festival held on the 15th day of the 7th month in the lunar calendar, when the gates of Hell were open to allow Hungry Ghosts to roam in search of food. Did you talk to your friends in rural Canada about any of this while you were growing up?

My mom came over from China during the cultural revolution, and my dad came over from Hong Kong around the same time in the 70’s. So they came from a place that coincided with the older world, and they brought with them the old stories. Often those stories involved the spiritual realms.

When I was growing up in Red Deer, Alberta, we were essentially one of 2 or 3 Chinese families in the city so it was kind of difficult to bring up any of these rituals or stories in a way that made sense to them, because it didn’t really make sense to me. As a kid I very much kept those worlds separate, perhaps because of fear or embarrassment. I’m not really sure. But that’s why this book is so important to me now. It gave me an opportunity to reconcile and embrace where and what I came from.

From ‘Blank Notes’ by Marshall To, published by Charcoal Press

What made you decide you wanted to capture this unseen world in photographs?

At the beginning I was just photographing because I enjoyed it, not thinking too much about it at all. But then came the purpose and possibility of a book. Through the many mind opening occasions at Chico Review, I was able to begin thinking of possibilities of making something uniquely my own, the countless books, artists and movies I was exposed to really gave me the imagination of what I could create. I decided to reconcile and embrace all my experiences as a Chinese Canadian and tell a new story that is inspired by all the old stories.

From ‘Blank Notes’ by Marshall To, published by Charcoal Press

You did a beautiful job capturing the supernatural world. Can you tell me a bit about your approach. It looks like you mainly shot at night or in fog. Did you have specific animals or person or scenes in mind, or did you wander around hoping the spirits would find you?

At first it began with trying to conquer the fear of the dark, wandering parks at night trying to capture animals as most of them are more active at night. I chose animals that I found fascinating and did a bit of research on which animals were important in Asian cultures.

Once I stayed in the dark long enough for the fear to pass, it became so peaceful. The anxieties of the day don’t seem as primal as the anxieties of the night.

I was told as a child not to do anything disrespectful during the festival nights as there was a chance that those who wander and have no families might follow you home. So still to this day, I try not to do any disrespectful things at night, even on non-festival nights. I’m definitely not trying to find spirits, because there’s a part of me that believes that they might be everywhere and it makes me truly afraid.

From ‘Blank Notes’ by Marshall To, published by Charcoal Press

Did this change at all your relation to nature or how you think of the supernatural world? What was your family’s reaction to this photobook?

I think it did change my relationship with both. As for nature, I see this incredibly old world that has been there before us and has seen it all and that includes the supernatural world which to me coincides with nature.

My family has had such a supportive reaction to my photobook. I’m not sure they necessarily understand it, but I’m not sure if I completely understand it. So yeah, they’ve given me every opportunity to make this work, and that’s all I can every ask for.

The cover of ‘Blank Notes’ by Marshall To, published by Charcoal Press

Is there anything else you would like to add?

For those who are wishing to pursue art in the world: Pursue openness, pursue grace and pursue failure.

article_text:
この度、初のTokyo Art Beatが主催するフリーマーケット 「ART BEAT FLEA-MARKET（略称：ABF／エビフ）」 を12月6日（日）、神保町の New Gallery にて開催します。

アートが好きな人たちが、ゆるやかに交流できる場所

これまでTokyo Art Beatでは、展覧会やアートにまつわる情報をオンラインを中心にお届けしてきました。だからこそ、日頃よりTokyo Art Beatを楽しんでくださっているみなさんと、気軽に顔を合わせて交流できる場をつくりたいと考え、ART BEAT FLEA-MARKETを開催します。 本フリーマーケットでは、様々な立場でアートに関わる出店者が参加します。私物やZINE、古本、雑貨、オリジナルグッズ、古着など、それぞれの視点で選んだアイテムが並びます。普段の活動だけでは見えてこない出店者それぞれの興味や関心に触れられるのもABFならではの楽しみです。 フリーマーケットという形だからこそ、ものを見たり、手に取ったり、買ったりしながら自然と会話が生まれる。出店者と来場者が気軽に会話を楽しみながら、交流を楽しめる場になればと思っています。

出店者 紹介

・絶感馬（ぜっかんま） 絶/ze̞Q/ - unparalleled 感 /kaɴ/ - sense 馬/ma/ - horse By KAITO Itsuki and Kazquiz 北海道枝幸郡枝幸町風烈布番外地 With piñata and Yugo Takayama 主な出品予定：ZINE、古本、リソグラフ、古着、グッズ

・木下理子 美術作家。2019年 武蔵野美術大学大学院 修士課程 油絵コース修了。水彩や日光写真などの技法を用いたドローイング、身近な素材を使用した立体、空間的なアプローチで作品を制作している。 主な出品予定：写真のマグネット、絵のハギレ封筒、美術系古本

・板坂留五 2018年に店舗兼住宅《半麦ハット》をきっかけに独立し、RUI Architectsを設立しました。建築設計を軸に、プロダクトや素材開発、建物、作品制作まで、大きさにかかわらない活動を行っています。 当日は、過去のプロジェクトから派生したオリジナル家具や、趣味で作っているTシャツなど、公私混ぜこぜでお待ちしています！ 主な出品予定：ZINEやプロダクト、家具など

・ザ・フー ザ・フーは、キュレーターのMIO、俳優のMIYU、アーティストのMEGAの3人からなるアーティスト・コレクティブ。2022年以降それぞれの道を歩んでいたが、この度再始動！等身大のフェミニズム・メッセージをZINEやプロダクト、Instagramなどを通じて発信していきます♡ 主な出品予定：新作ZINE、新作ステッカー、既刊ZINE（27 ZINE、OPPAI ZINE）、オリジナルマスキングテープ

・ Open Letter アートを通して「問い」をひらくプロジェクトハウス。2015年にスタートし、現在は杉並区上北沢の古民家をDIY改装した住まい兼ギャラリーで活動しています。都市の中で生活の場をパブリックにひらき、日常と展示が地続きになった親密な対話の場をつくっています。当日はオリジナルグッズや蔵書、ZINEに加え、店主の偏向・偏愛たっぷりの私物も持参予定です。ぜひブースで気軽にお声がけください！ 主な出品予定：オリジナルZINE、オリジナルトート、オリジナルTシャツ、娘（6歳）のZINE、私物のZINE、私物のアートブック

・八木宏基（HARMAS GALLERY）八木美和子（PARLOUR HARMAS） 清澄白河エリアで現代美術のギャラリーをやっています。今年移転して現代美術館に近くなりました！ 主な出品予定：植物、焼き菓子、食器、本、インテリア小物

・灯明 荒川区西尾久でアーティストの冨樫達彦が2020年から営む居酒屋。同スペース内に国内外の同時代のアーティストの展覧会を企画するギャラリーLavender Opener Chairを併設している。 主な出品予定：器、グラス、香水、古着、時計

・大平かりん 編集者。「365日同じコーディネートはしない」をモットーに、インスタグラムで更新している私服にはファンが多い。日本カルチャーやクリエイティブの最前線を築いてきたゲストを迎えるポッドキャスト番組『大平かりんの門外談』のホストを務める。 主な出品予定：ディース古着、デザイナーズアイテム

当日は、出店者のみなさんに加えてTokyo Art Beatのスタッフも私物を持ち寄り出店します。記事やサービスからは伝わらない、スタッフの個性に触れられる機会となれば幸いです。どんなものを持ち寄るのか、お楽しみに！Tokyo Art Beatのオリジナルグッズも販売予定。

会員向け特典

会場にご来場いただいたTokyo Art Beat会員の方には、無料でオリジナルグッズをプレゼント予定！詳細は後日発表予定です。

開催日：12月6日（日） 時間：11:00〜19:00（予定） 会場：New Gallery（〒101-0051 東京都千代田区神田神保町1-28-1 1F）

article_text:
Chinese artist and filmmaker Sun Xun never expected “ Magic Atlas ” to become the first animated feature selected for the Tokyo International Film Festival ’s competition.

“I never thought of ‘Magic Atlas’ as an animated film. To me, it brings together many art forms. Animation is simply the label we use for its form. I’m glad people at TIFF understood the effort I put into it,” Sun tells Variety .

Related Stories

Quentin Tarantino Surprises Fans With 17 Minutes of ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’ at AFI Fest

Sanjay Gupta, Indian Director of 'Kaante' and 'Zinda,' Dies at 59

“Magic Atlas,” a decade in the making, is set in Luocha, a coal-mining empire where flying is forbidden. Every 60 years, a festival leaves the population unable to remember the era that came before. After a magician is arrested, he meets an orphan boy in prison and gives him the Magic Atlas. The book points the boy toward a past the empire has tried to erase.

The film moves between woodblock prints, ink painting and vivid color. Its images often do the work that a conventional plot might spell out, drawing on art and visual traditions from different periods and cultures.

Sun says the film was shaped by global events, including the pandemic and the war in Ukraine, as well as personal changes such as his conversion to Buddhism. He put all his savings into the project. When galleries shut down during the pandemic, his art sales dried up. He says he had to find buyers himself and take out loans to keep the film going.

“In my own artistic thinking, I believe every creator should have one ‘all-in’ moment in their life: to make a defining work that takes everything out of them. For me, ‘Magic Atlas’ was that all-in moment,” he says. “I hoped to finish it before my child grew up and while my parents were still alive. Sadly, my father passed away a year before the film was completed.”

Rather than comment on any one event, Sun says, he drew on different cultural and political influences to reflect the divisions he sees around the world. He also brought in images of ancient civilizations, including the pyramids, alongside mythological elements.

“Film cannot address reality directly, but it can take a wider view. It can express how we understand the world and what we are curious about,” he says.

Asked whether films need to explain their stories clearly, Sun says: “I’m actually against ‘story.’ I don’t mean that films shouldn’t have stories. I object to films that emphasize story for the sake of packaging and commercial purposes. As an art form, film should express a state of being.”

Sun names Andrei Tarkovsky, citing 1983’s “Nostalghia,” and the late Hungarian filmmaker Béla Tarr as filmmakers he admires. “They are sincere in the way they approach existence. They don’t rely only on imagined narratives. To me, that is the kind of artistic form cinema should have,” he says.

While working on “Magic Atlas,” Sun studied Dunhuang murals, Song dynasty painting and calligraphy, along with imagery from other cultures. Asked if he worries that some viewers might find the film difficult to follow, he says: “There will always be a barrier to entry. Ten years of work naturally gives the film depth. But I made this important work for myself. My goal was to realize it, not to please every viewer.”

Sun says exhibitions connected to “Magic Atlas” are planned in the U.S. and Singapore, though venues and dates have not been unveiled. He has also begun a new feature he calls “All or Nothing,” whose Mandarin title, “Fuyou,” means “Mayfly.” The film will continue the world of “Magic Atlas,” moving from the broad theme of forgetting to an individual experience of memory loss. Sun says he filmed the first shot at an exhibition space in Hangzhou and hopes to finish the feature within two years.

editorial_title_zh: 共同物质：玛丽内拉·塞纳托雷作品中参与的力量
editorial_excerpt_zh: 一个陶瓷整体赋予了马尔卡·科罗纳员工的共享声音与经历以形态。通过《共同物质》，玛丽内拉·塞纳托雷将参与转化为艺术作品。本文《共同物质：玛丽内拉·塞纳托雷作品中参与的力量》源自……
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "参与并非把几个人凑到一个房间里。它不是一个空洞的词汇，而是一种精神、心灵和身心的投入，其中合唱般的共鸣让个性得以绽放。这是由玛丽内拉·塞纳托雷与陶瓷企业马尔卡·科罗纳（Marca Corona）的员工在第五届“马尔卡·科罗纳艺术计划”（Marca Corona per l’Arte）之际共同创作的作品的基础手势与标志。", "links": [{"text": "ceramiche Marca Corona", "url": "https://www.marcacorona.it/it/?gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=23993061492&gbraid=0AAAAACgGx-rz92RWTuwfA1t5dZm4ojm9o&gclid=CjwKCAjwuobXBhBXEiwAYUaIlW4rCDuWXwNfmutKUn44PEepJw-nwpHjD2OylC02x4Jc2UFshhgroxoCbv8QAvD_BwE"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "该项目将一直展出至2026年12月4日，它融入了对马尔卡·科罗纳历史的当代重新解读中。该公司于1741年成立于萨苏洛，最初是一家艺术陶瓷和装饰品制造商，随后在20世纪临近时专注于瓷砖生产。通过邀请自2022年起连续几届的活动主角——如朱塞佩·斯坦波内（Giuseppe Stampone）、斯特凡诺·阿里恩蒂（Stefano Arienti）、安德烈亚·马斯特罗维托（Andrea Mastrovito）和皮诺·德奥达托（Pino Deodato）等当代艺术家，该倡议将艺术实践带入了企业的日常生活中，使工作社区成为创作过程的积极参与者。然而，正如马尔卡·科罗纳首席执行官莱利奥·庞切米（Lelio Poncemi）所强调的那样，“玛丽内拉·塞纳托雷与马尔卡·科罗纳员工之间的关系之所以意义重大，首先且最主要是因为她的工作方式”。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/MarinellaSenatore_BodiesInAlliance_22_InstallationViewMarcaCorona_CourtesyArtistaEMazzoleni_PhMazenJannoun-1-1024x994.jpg", "alt": "marinella senatore marca corona ", "caption": "Marinella Senatore, Bodies in Alliance, 2022, installation view, Ceramiche Marca Corona, lampadine LED, alluminio e basamento in legno su struttura in acciaio 274 x 340 x 164 cm. Courtesy l’Artista e Mazzoleni Photo: Mazen Jannoun", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "通过面向所有员工（从管理层到行政、商业、生产和物流部门）开放的阅读、集体写作和身体律动工作坊，玛丽内拉·塞纳托雷带来了她自身的艺术行囊，将愿望、经历和抱负转化为一件集体作品：在工作坊的过程中，参与者通过语言、文本和相互倾听的时刻分享了他们各自经历的各个方面，并与引导式的身体练习交织在一起。事实上，实验室阶段被构想为作品真正的创造性和奠基性行为，作品的意义正是在此显现，随后由艺术家将其塑造成最终的图像。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/MarinellaSenatore_BreatheUAreEnough_22_InstallationViewMarcaCorona_CourtesyArtistaEMazzoleni_PhMazenJannoun-1-1024x819.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Marinella Senatore, Breathe, U Are Enough, 2022, installation view, Ceramiche Marca Corona, tubi di vetro con miscela di gas priva di mercurio (greeNeon) e metacrilato colato, montati su pannello in acciaio verniciato. article_text:
Partecipazione non è mettere insieme delle persone in una stanza. Non è una parola vuota, ma un impegno mentale, spirituale e somatico, in cui la coralità fa fiorire l’individualità. È il gesto e il segno alla base dell’opera realizzata da Marinella Senatore insieme ai dipendenti dell’azienda di ceramiche Marca Corona , in occasione della V edizione del progetto Marca Corona per l’Arte.

Visitabile fino al 4 dicembre 2026, il progetto si inserisce in un percorso di rilettura contemporanea della storia di Marca Corona, fondata a Sassuolo nel 1741 come manifattura di ceramiche artistiche e oggetti decorativi, prima di specializzarsi, a ridosso del XX secolo, nella produzione di piastrelle. Attraverso il coinvolgimento di artisti contemporanei, come Giuseppe Stampone, Stefano Arienti, Andrea Mastrovito e Pino Deodato , protagonisti delle edizioni succedutesi dal 2022, l’iniziativa porta la pratica artistica nella quotidianità dell’impresa, rendendo la comunità di lavoro parte attiva del processo creativo. Come sottolinea Lelio Poncemi , Amministratore Delegato di Marca Corona, però, «quello tra Marinella Senatore e i dipendenti di Marca Corona è stato un rapporto significativo anche e soprattutto per il modo con cui lei lavora».

Attraverso un workshop di lettura, scrittura collettiva e movimento somatico aperto a tutti i dipendenti, dal management alle aree amministrative, commerciali, produttive e logistiche, Marinella Senatore porta il proprio bagaglio artistico traducendo in un’opera collettiva desideri, esperienze e aspirazioni: nel corso del workshop, i partecipanti hanno condiviso aspetti della propria esperienza attraverso parole, testi e momenti di ascolto reciproco, intrecciati a esercizi somatici guidati. Il momento laboratoriale viene infatti concepito come il vero e proprio atto creativo e fondativo dell’opera, in cui il senso della stessa emerge, per poi essere plasmato in un’immagine finale dall’artista.

Ne è nato Materia Comune , un grande monolite in ceramica di 3,6 × 1,8 metri, che dà forma concreta all’esperienza. Come sottolinea Mariacristina Ferraioli , è «un’opera costruita dall’azienda, nell’azienda e con l’azienda»: un monumento che non è monos , unità isolata, ma celebrazione di una comunità. Il titolo stesso richiama questa dimensione condivisa, in cui la materia diventa il punto d’incontro tra le singole esperienze e un’identità collettiva. Ogni partecipante trova posto nell’opera: o sul fronte, nella composizione, o sul retro, dove sono raccolti pensieri e parole emersi durante gli scambi.

Il lavoro accosta il collage, tecnica ampiamente impiegata nella pratica di Senatore, alla ceramica, materiale centrale per l’azienda ma del tutto inedito per lei, un binomio che mette in luce tanto la porosità e la natura aperta della sua ricerca quanto le possibilità espressive della materia. Sulla superficie emergono le sagome di persone e di una mano, richiamo al lavoro manuale e al contatto, gesto originario della relazione. Sullo sfondo si dispongono motivi floreali, ricorrenti nella ricerca dell’artista. Anche la palette cromatica, dai toni terrosi, è il risultato di questo confronto. Senatore ha raccontato di aver inizialmente immaginato colori diversi, poi ripensati attraverso l’incontro con la sensibilità e l’identità dell’azienda: nell’opera risuona lo sforzo collettivo e le energie interne all’azienda, e un inno alla ceramica, che «trasforma la terra in eternità».

Passeggiando poi tra le sale della Galleria Marca Corona, nata nel 2010, si coglie il dialogo tra la ricerca contemporanea di Senatore e le ceramiche della collezione storica dell’azienda, nata come «Fabbrica della Majolica», e confermata nel tempo come la più antica azienda di ceramica del territorio. Alle luminarie dell’artista, collocate sia negli spazi interni che esterni dell’azienda, risponde la maestria decorativa delle manifatture del passato, al collage si affiancano brocche e piatti riccamente ornati. Accostamenti che restituiscono l’immagine di un’azienda capace di confrontarsi con la propria storia senza cristallizzarsi, aperta a nuove interpretazioni e sensibilità.

Materia Comune si propone come un manifesto della collettività, un totem che custodisce la memoria di un’esperienza condivisa e ne rende tangibile la forza. Un segno che ricorda come la partecipazione sia non soltanto possibile, ma necessaria nel nostro presente: per creare legami, sentirsi parte di una rete e riconoscersi come presenze attive, insostituibili, mai superflue all’interno di una comunità.

editorial_title_zh: 明星电影票房惨败与投资放缓有助解释中国在电影节上存在感减弱，东京电影节节目总监如是说

"text": "在他看来，这些电影人大多是在回首过去的事件，以此作为审视一个日益分裂的世界的一种方式。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "东京电影节的主竞赛单元要求至少达到亚洲首映级别，但该片节一直力争世界首映，这两者之间的比例通常各占一半左右。电影节还力求大约一半的15部影片来自亚洲。有望塑造世界电影未来的新锐导演会受到优先考虑，地位确立的名导也不会被拒之门外，尽管老牌导演并未被排除在外。今年的片单包括加林·努格罗和（Garin Nugroho，代表作《黎明前夕》）、米尔科·曼切夫斯基（Milcho "“我们希望我们的竞赛单元能够成为一个发掘新人的平台，”他说道。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "入围主竞赛单元的日本本土影片包括池田明（Ikeda Akira）的《金丝雀的摇篮曲》（The Canary’s Lullaby）和山本明（Yamamoto Akira）的《交织》（The Intertwining），它们与“日本电影现状”（Nippon Cinema Now）单元的影片一同亮相。市山尚三评价这些电影人迄今尚未享有国际声誉，但他们理应获得全球的认可。作为特别展映单元的日本电影，包括开幕影片由濑濑敬久（Zeze Takahisa）执导的《寿喜烧》（Sukiyaki）、山崎贵（Yamazaki Takashi）的《哥斯拉-1.0》（Godzilla Minus "“这表明日本电影的现状非常健康。我认为日本有数量惊人之多的才华横溢的电影人。当务之急是为年轻导演的电影提供支持，其中许多电影的制作预算非常低，”市山尚三说道。“虽然过去几年各方对日本电影的支持以各种形式有所增加，但对低成本电影的支持仍然不够。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "市山尚三在担任节目总监之前，曾指出东京缺乏全球许多电影节所具备的两个要素：对电影制作的资金支持，以及培养行业未来人才的教育项目。在他看来，釜山是亚洲第一个同时引入这两项内容的电影节。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "东京目前正在努力缩小这一差距。去年，它推出了亚洲学生电影节（Asian Students’ Film Conference），放映来自东亚和东南亚的学生作品；今年，它又增设了TIFF在建项目（TIFF Work-in-Progress），这是一个旨在为寻求资金完成制作的日本电影提供支持的项目。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“当然，这还远远不够，”市山尚三说。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他表示，未来五年的任务是进一步推进这一方法。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
Star-driven flops at the Chinese box office, slowing investment and a reportedly more complicated censorship process have a bearing on China’s low profile at international festivals this year, according to Ichiyama Shozo , programming director of the Tokyo International Film Festival .

“In the past, casting a star in the leading role could guarantee a certain degree of success, but this year, many films featuring star actors have flopped at the box office,” Ichiyama tells Variety .

Investment has slowed, he says, and many titles are reportedly sitting unreleased as censorship has grown more complex. All of that, in his view, has something to do with the absence of a strong Chinese showing on the festival circuit in 2026.

Popular on Variety

Ichiyama has worked closely with Chinese-language auteurs including Hou Hsiao-hsien and Jia Zhangke, and says the mainland industry changed sharply in the mid-2000s. As the economy boomed, multiplexes multiplied and box office prospects rose, even independent projects with no stars attached could raise reasonable budgets in China.

Taiwan, by contrast, looks comparatively steady. Its home market has always been small, Ichiyama says, but a range of public support mechanisms keeps production going.

This year’s lineup is marked by films about historical events, wars among them, Ichiyama says. They include Samuele Rossi’s Competition entry “Even If Hell Came,” which follows a young Italian partisan holding out in the Alps in the winter of 1944.

“I believe this reflects a global trend, as symbolized by the films dealing with the Second World War that were screened at this year’s Cannes Film Festival,” he says.

Most of these filmmakers, he believes, look back at past events as a way to examine a world that is growing more divided.

Tokyo’s Competition requires at least an Asian premiere, but the festival pushes for world premieres, and the split between the two usually lands at around half and half. The festival also aims for around half of the 15 films to come from Asia. Emerging directors expected to shape the future of world cinema get priority over established names, though veterans are not shut out. This year’s lineup includes veterans such as Garin Nugroho (“Red Before Dawn”), Milcho Manchevski (“Sister Brother Manhole Cover”) and Bahman Ghobadi (“Trees Are Watching”). Ichiyama says the established directors in the selection are reaching for something different from their earlier work.

“We hope that our competition will serve as a platform for discovery,” he says.

The Japanese titles in Competition, among them Ikeda Akira’s “The Canary’s Lullaby” and Yamamoto Akira’s “The Intertwining,” sit alongside those in the Nippon Cinema Now section. Ichiyama describes these filmmakers as lacking an international reputation so far but deserving of worldwide recognition. The Japanese films in the Gala Selection, including opener “Sukiyaki” from Zeze Takahisa, Yamazaki Takashi’s “Godzilla Minus Zero” and Sode Yukiko’s “All the Lovers in the Night,” work with bigger budgets and commercial demands while holding on to an auteur sensibility.

“This demonstrates that the current state of Japanese cinema is in a very healthy condition. I think there are a surprisingly large number of talented filmmakers in Japan. The immediate challenge is to provide support for films by young directors, many of which are produced on a very low budget,” Ichiyama says. “While support for Japanese cinema has increased in various forms over the past few years, support for low-budget films is still insufficient.”

Before Ichiyama became programming director, Tokyo lacked, he says, two things many festivals worldwide offer: backing for film production and education programs to train the industry’s future talent. Busan, in his view, was the first festival in Asia to introduce both.

Tokyo is now trying to close that gap. Last year it launched the Asian Students’ Film Conference, which screens student work from East and Southeast Asia, and this year it added TIFF Work-in-Progress, a program for Japanese films looking for money to finish production.

“Of course, this is not yet enough,” Ichiyama says.

The task for the next five years, he says, is to take that approach further.

article_text:
Deep Shadows: Online Halloween Exhibition

©Mikayla David, Untitled, Richmond, VA, https://davidmi.myportfolio.com/, @soggyartss

Happy Halloween!

Thank you to all the talented photographers who submitted their work to Deep Shadows , an online exhibition celebrating the mysteries of Halloween. Drawing from urban legends, Victorian-era lore, and the uncanny, the selected images evoke nostalgia and unease through haunting portraits, strange landscapes, and allusions to magic. Selecting just fifty photographs from hundreds of submissions was a challenge. Each chosen image invites viewers into a world where stories unfold through suggestion and ambiguity, revealing how much can be communicated by limiting what is seen and leaving the rest to the imagination.

editorial_excerpt_zh: 夏安·海德获得奥斯卡奖的《健听女孩》感觉像是一部不属于这个时代的电影。它正是那种米拉麦克斯在几十年前就会推向颁奖季成功的通俗大众向作品，我认为它之所以能在学院斩获佳绩，只是因为投票者们对那种……
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "夏安·海德获得奥斯卡奖的《健听女孩》感觉像是一部不属于这个时代的电影。它正是那种米拉麦克斯在几十年前就会推向颁奖季成功的通俗大众向作品，我认为它之所以能在学院斩获佳绩，只是因为投票者们对那种随着韦恩斯坦兄弟淡出而消失的美国独立电影怀有一种安静的怀旧情绪。当把它当作对聋哑社群生活的真实、接地气的描绘来审视时，它显然经不起推敲；影片对他们面临的诸多挑战进行了简化和还原式的尝试，通过非听力受损的家庭女儿这一观众代入视角来构建时，带有太强的局外人视角，让人频频出戏。因此，当海德接下来执导一部更明确以残疾人权利行动主义为主题的电影时，自然让我敲响了警钟，但《做赫曼》在平衡其讨好观众的本能与融入角色的日常抗争视角方面做得要出色得多，它从不让观众觉得自己是在局外窥探。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "改编自残疾人权利活动家朱迪斯·赫曼同名自传（书名带有一点尴尬的双关），《做赫曼》并不是那种宣传中所呈现的电影。如果你看过那些吹嘘着“改编自一场真正的革命”这一尴尬宣传语的市场物料，你就会做好准备去期待一部远比实际成品更具凯旋色彩的电影——即便它带有让人联想起米拉麦克斯的声望基调（你可以想象他们的颁奖季宣传会要求投票者“向这位女性致敬，向这部电影致敬”），它对这里通过法律确立的权利之局限性也并非天真无知。围绕1977年在旧金山卫生部办公室由赫曼（露丝·梅德利饰）组织的长达28天的静坐抗议展开结构，其叙事核心是这位活动家为确保1973年《康复法案》第504条能够被立法者签署而进行的奋斗。这是针对残疾人的首个联邦民权保护法案，确保任何被视为歧视的政府资助项目都无法获得资金，但在撰写多年后，它迟迟未能变成现实。由于让每一座联邦建筑都实现无障碍改造需要数十亿美元的成本，历届政府不断将皮球踢给未来，吉米·卡特政府在其早期也没有表现出任何改变这一现状的迹象。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "即便你之前并不了解这位活动家的努力，你也知道结局如何；无障碍轮椅坡道在公共空间中已经存在了太久，以至于我们大多数人可能根本没有想过，让它们出现在那里最初曾经经历过一场斗争。自然，当卫生部长约瑟夫·A·卡利法诺（马克·鲁法洛饰）最终签署立法时，我们会觉得自己正被引导迎来一个凯旋的结局，但海德从未失去对宏观全景的关注。她的主角并没有停下来庆祝任何胜利，她也要求观众效仿这一点，她清醒地认识到每一个里程碑式的法律突破并不标志着幸福结局的到来，而且几十年后仍然存在着需要正视的巨大不平等。这是对这位女性以及帮助将这些民权问题带入健全人世界视野的同道活动家们的庆祝，但从未将他们定位为除了需要倒下的第一张多米诺骨牌之外的任何角色。对于一部旨在迎合大众的凯旋向电影来说，这是一种令人钦佩的非同寻常的处理方式，对赫曼的性格刻画亦是如此——她是一个甚至连同行倡导者都觉得极难相处的人，经常要求他们为了继续抗议而忽略自身医疗状况的需求。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《做赫曼》最大的成功或许在于它如何处理残疾人权利的交叉性这一主题，以及在平衡看似对立的不同群体需求时所产生的艰难对话。同样，我们知道这些紧张关系是如何开始得到解决的，但将它们戏剧化呈现的过程依然具有一种迷人之处。在其实现得最充分的时候，抗议者之间关于如何确保他们各自不同的需求得以实现、以及与其他哪些组织结盟才是安全的辩论，让人联想起罗宾·坎皮略的《每分钟120击》中艾滋病活动家之间紧张的行政市政厅会议。这部电影过于精致且好莱坞化，不足以让人做进一步的对比来媲美那部杰作，但这些短暂的惊鸿一瞥表明，海德与联合编剧丽贝卡·陶西格正在效仿那部电影的做法，确保各种不同的真实生活视角都能获得平等的倾听时间。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": article_text:
Sian Heder’s Oscar winner CODA felt like a movie out of time. It was the kind of broad crowd-pleaser that Miramax would have released to awards success a couple of decades earlier, which I would argue only triumphed with the Academy as voters were quietly nostalgic for the kind of American indie that disappeared alongside the Weinsteins. It certainly didn’t hold up to scrutiny as a lived-in, authentic account of the deaf community, with its simplistic and reductive attempt to chronicle their many challenges feeling too distractingly like an outsider’s perspective when framed through the audience surrogate of the family’s non-hearing-impaired daughter. For Heder to follow it with a tale more explicitly about disability-rights activism naturally got my alarm bells ringing, but Being Heumann does a far better job balancing its audience-satisfying instincts with an embedded perspective of its characters’ everyday struggles, never allowing the viewer to feel on the outside looking in.

Adapted from disability-rights activist Judith Heumann’s autobiography of the same cringily punning name, Being Heumann isn’t quite the movie that’s been advertised. If you’ve seen the marketing that’s boasted the awkward tagline “based on a true revolution,” you’ll be primed to expect a movie far more triumphant than what’s delivered, which, even with its Miramax-reminiscent prestige tone (you can imagine their awards campaign asking voters to “honor the woman, honor the film”), isn’t naive about the limitations of the rights enshrined into law here. Structured around the 28-day sit-in Heumann (Ruth Madeley) organized at the Department of Health offices in San Francisco in 1977, its narrative is centered on the activist’s quest to ensure Section 504 of the 1973 Rehabilitation Act would be signed by lawmakers. It was the first federal civil-rights protection for people with disabilities, ensuring no government-funded program would receive money if seen to discriminate, but it hadn’t been ushered into reality years after being written. Successive governments kept kicking the can down the road due to the multi-billion-dollar cost of making every federal building accessible, and nothing about Jimmy Carter’s administration suggested otherwise in its early days.

Even if you weren’t previously aware of the activist’s efforts, you know how this ends; wheelchair-accessible ramps have been commonplace in public spaces for so long, most of us probably haven’t considered there was a fight to get them there in the first place. Naturally, it feels like we’re being primed for a triumphant finale when health secretary Joseph A. Califano (Mark Ruffalo) finally signs the legislation, but Heder never loses sight of the bigger picture. Her protagonist doesn’t pause to celebrate any win, and she asks her audience to follow suit, self-aware that each milestone legal breakthrough doesn’t mark a happy ending and that there are still vast inequalities decades later which need to be reckoned with. It’s a celebration of the woman and fellow activists who helped bring these civil-rights issues to the able-bodied world’s attention, but never positions them as anything more than the first domino which needed to fall. This is an admirably unusual approach for a triumphalist crowd-pleaser, as is the characterization of Heumann as someone who was very difficult even for her fellow advocates to deal with, often asking them to overlook the needs of their own medical conditions for the sake of continuing their protest.

Maybe the biggest success of Being Heumann is how it approaches the topic of disability-rights intersectionality and the difficult conversations that arise from balancing the needs of people with different conditions that seem opposing. Again, we know how these tensions began to be resolved, but there’s a fascination to seeing them dramatized. At their most strongly realized, debates amongst the protesters about how to ensure their disparate needs come to fruition and which other organizations are safe to ally with are reminiscent of the tense administrative town hall meetings between the AIDS activists in Robin Campillo’s BPM . The movie is far too polished and Hollywood to invite further comparisons to that stellar piece of work, but the brief glimpses show that Heder and co-screenwriter Rebekah Taussig are following that film’s lead in ensuring the wide variety of lived-in perspectives are given equal time to be heard.

This approach also extends to the way they feel reluctant to outwardly depict Califano as a cartoonish villain, instead dramatizing him as more of an establishment weasel who is only reluctant to sign legislation because he expects to be fired for greenlighting such a costly program. He’s not opposed to the expansion of civil rights to aid the disabled, but prioritizes his job security over signing the dotted line, constantly arguing that marching in Selma with MLK is proof of his overall good intentions. Judging from the current state of the Democratic party, especially in the recent Joe Biden administration, his platitude-driven inaction has proven influential to a new class of career politicians, and a stronger movie would take a more cynical approach here. It’s refreshing that his characterization is more developed than a one-note villain, reflecting the real bureaucratic obstacles Heumann had to contend with, but this is still a broad crowdpleaser that’ll likely wind up in Barack Obama’s end-of year list; the better version of this story would reflect the stasis in civil rights breakthroughs even after Heumann served in his administration.

Some side characters also feel underdeveloped––Dylan O’Brien’s reporter Evan White goes from dismissive and vaguely prejudiced to an active supporter seemingly offscreen, between scenes––but it’s easy to argue that, like Heumann herself, the movie is ultimately too focused on the bigger picture to afford them much weight. It still manages to be rousing despite these flaws, the familiarity of its comfortable tone making it easier to commend the ways it breaks from the Miramax formula. This isn’t a naive depiction of a triumph against the system, but rather a small, hard-won administrative victory within a system that kept putting up new roadblocks long after it passed. In that regard, it’s about as grounded as a Hollywoodized iteration of this narrative could be.

Being Heumann screened at the 2026 BFI London Film Festival and opens in theaters on November 6 and arrives on Apple TV on November 13.

title_original: Patrick Graham, Cathy Wilkes Win Inaugural Bacon Awards
editorial_title_zh: 帕特里克·格雷厄姆和凯茜·威尔克斯赢得首届培根奖
editorial_excerpt_zh: 44,800美元的奖金将在两位艺术家之间平分。
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "爱尔兰艺术家帕特里克·格雷厄姆（Patrick Graham）和北爱尔兰艺术家凯茜·威尔克斯（Cathy Wilkes）成为首届爱尔兰视觉艺术弗朗西斯·培根奖（Francis Bacon Awards for Irish Visual Arts）的得主。", "links": [{"text": "Francis Bacon", "url": "https://www.artnews.com/t/francis-bacon/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "格雷厄姆因其对爱尔兰绘画的贡献以及在六个多十年中对当代视觉艺术的影响而获得弗朗西斯·培根终身成就奖，而威尔克斯则因其涵盖雕塑、绘画、素描和装置的多重身份创作实践而获得弗朗西斯·培根中期艺术家奖。40,000欧元（44,800美元）的奖金将被平分，格雷厄姆将获得25,000欧元，威尔克斯将获得15,000欧元。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "两位艺术家将在2026年都柏林画廊周末（Dublin Gallery Weekend 2026）期间被授奖，该活动于11月5日至8日举行。该奖项计划得到了拉克斯多城堡（Château La Coste）和亚德利·戈达德律师事务所（Addleshaw Goddard）的支持。作为奖项的一部分，格雷厄姆和威尔克斯将应邀在法国普罗旺斯的拉克斯多城堡举办个展。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在评选获奖者时，主办方成立了一个国际评审团，成员包括伦敦伏尔泰工作室（Studio Voltaire）主席艾玛·戈尔茨（Emma Goltz）；都柏林休·莱恩画廊（Hugh Lane Gallery）馆长芭芭拉·道森（Barbara Dawson）；海沃德巡回画廊（Hayward Touring Gallery）负责人布赖恩·卡斯（Brian Cass）；作家、评论家兼教育家卡维欣·麦克·吉奥拉·莱斯（Caoimhín Mac Giolla Léith），以及科克克劳福德美术馆（Crawford Art Gallery）馆长玛丽·麦卡锡（Mary McCarthy）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "评审团赞扬格雷厄姆推动了1980年代具象绘画的复兴，并指出他最有力的作品将“对肉体本能的刻画与哀怨文字的零星片段结合在一起——直面文化创伤、宗教压抑和存在主义焦虑”。威尔克斯的作品则因其“带伤的美感与脆弱的优雅”以及她在创作中对“日常材料”的运用而受到赞誉。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "为了纪念2026年都柏林画廊周末，由罗伯特·戴安特（Robert Diament）和拉塞尔·托维（Russell Tovey）主持的播客节目《Talk Art》将于11月7日在爱尔兰国家美术馆进行现场录制，与格雷厄姆一起探讨他对当代爱尔兰绘画的影响及其长达六十年的职业生涯。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
Irish artist Patrick Graham and Northern Irish artist Cathy Wilkes are the recipients of the inaugural Francis Bacon Awards for Irish Visual Arts program.

Graham is being awarded the Francis Bacon Lifetime Achievement Award for his contribution to Irish painting and influence on contemporary visual art over more than six decades, while Wilkes is receiving the Francis Bacon Mid-Career Artist Award, nodding to her multihyphenated practice of sculpture, painting, drawing and installation. The €40,000 ($44,800) prize fund is being split, Graham will receive €25,000 and €15,000 for Wilkes.

Both artists will be awarded during Dublin Gallery Weekend 2026, taking place from November 5 through to 8. The award program has been supported by Château La Coste and the law firm Addleshaw Goddard. Graham and Wilkes will be invited to stage solo exhibitions at Château La Coste in Provence, France as part of the award.

In choosing the recipients of the award, an international judging panel was established with Emma Goltz, chair of Studio Voltaire in London; Barbara Dawson, director of Hugh Lane Gallery in Dublin; Brian Cass, head of the Hayward Touring Gallery at the Hayward Gallery; Caoimhín Mac Giolla Léith, writer, critic and educator, and Mary McCarthy, director of Crawford Art Gallery in Cork.

The judging panel praised Graham for the resurgence of figurative painting during the 1980s and that his most powerful work combined “visceral renderings of the mortal body with dispersed fragments of plaintive text – confronting cultural trauma, religious repression and existential angst.” Wilkes’ work was lauded for its “bruised beauty and fragile grace” and the use of “everyday materials” in her practice.

To commemorate the Dublin Gallery Weekend 2026, the podcast Talk Art, hosted by Robert Diament and Russell Tovey, will be recording live from the National Gallery of Ireland on November 7 with Graham to discuss his influence on contemporary Irish painting and his six-decade career.

article_text:
Tribeca prizewinner Darko Lungulov (“Here and There”) has wrapped production on “1970,” a coming-of-age drama set against the backdrop of President Nixon’s visit to the former Yugoslavia during the Vietnam War. The film will take part in the Agora Works in Progress strand at the Thessaloniki Film Festival before heading to Tallinn’s Baltic Event industry showcase later this month.

“1970” follows 13-year-old Draško, who — after being abandoned by his parents — runs away with the rebellious 16-year-old Eržika. Drifting from place to place, swept up amid a roiling climate of anti-war protests, rebellion, free love, wild rock concerts, drugs and decadent parties, his desperate journey home becomes an awakening of heartbreak, loss and freedom.

Related Stories

'The Vow' Trailer: Fox Nation Dating Show Has Chris Harrison, a Bachelor and 10 Women Looking for Love: 'Put a Baby in Me Now'

Fox Nation Plans to Place Promos for Chris Harrison's 'The Vow' on ABC Stations

The film is written and directed by Lungulov, who shares a producing credit with Snezana van Houwelingen. It’s produced by This and That Productions (Serbia), Papa Films (Serbia), Mirage Film (Hungary), Samsa Film (Luxembourg) and PomPom Film (Croatia), with financing and support from Film Center Serbia, the Hungarian National Film Institute, Film Fund Luxembourg, the Croatian Audiovisual Center, Film Fund Vojvodina and Creative Europe MEDIA.

Speaking to Variety in Thessaloniki, Lungulov explains that while his period drama is set more than 50 years in the past, “it is a story about today.”

“The film takes us to a time when young people believed they could change the world — something we seem to have forgotten,” the director says. Pointing to recent events in his native Serbia, where after two years of struggle, a student protest movement ousted longtime strongman Aleksandar Vučić last month, Lungulov says that “that possibility came incredibly to life again.”

The Belgrade-born director, who studied filmmaking in New York, is best known for “Here and There,” which won the Best NY Narrative Award at Tribeca in 2009 and was Serbia’s submission for the foreign-language Oscar that year. The film, which contrasted the adventures of an enterprising young Serbian in New York with the experiences of an aging New Yorker in Belgrade, was praised by Variety ’s Ronnie Scheib as a “laid-back character study [that] accrues small epiphanies with patient care, its mordant Eastern European humor tempered by a gentler sense of postwar absurdity.” His 2014 follow-up, the tragicomedy “Monument to Michael Jackson,” premiered at Karlovy Vary.

Lungulov’s last film was the 2023 documentary “A Fleeting Dream,” which followed the rock band Yu Grupa — a long-running musical act that, coincidentally, was formed in 1970. His latest will also incorporate documentary elements, with “1970” utilizing a mix of “real and fake home movies, newly shot 16mm and digital footage,” he says. “It is a film based on my own memories, and I wanted to create the hero’s inner world, his memories and the atmosphere of 1970 through the film’s internal language.”

Mirroring the political climate of that time, with raucous anti-Vietnam War protests greeting Nixon’s visit to Yugoslvaia, Lungulov notes that his two young leads — Andrija Femić, who plays Draško, and Lilla Gregus, who plays Eržika — were both “very active in the student movement” that brought down Vučić. At the time of filming, Gregus was a 22-year-old student at the Academy of Arts in Novi Sad, the Serbian town whose railway station disaster in 2024 jumpstarted the protest movement.

On one occasion, Lungulov himself joined the young actor and her fellow students at a demonstration after a rehearsal for “1970.” It’s that echo of the past in the present day, he says, that makes his film so timely.

“I feel this story is about today — young people searching for their voice in a hopeless world and refusing to be broken by bullying authorities, which feels like our last hope in today’s scary times,” he says. “And the Serbian students brought that hope back to us in Serbia, and perhaps to the world.”

The Thessaloniki Film Festival runs Nov. 5 – 15.

article_text:
Wie viel politische Macht darf ein Staat über die Bildung seiner Kinder haben? Mit dieser Problematik setzt sich ab 17. Oktober eine Ausstellung der 1986 geborenen, russisch-stämmigen, in Deutschland lebenden Autorin und Filmemacherin Yulia Lokshina in Pforzheim auseinander. Unter dem Titel „Active Vocabulary“ beleuchtet die Schau als begehbares interaktives Ausstellungsformat das Spannungsfeld zwischen Aufklärung und Indoktrination.

Ausgangspunkt der interdisziplinären, begehbaren Installation über drei Stockwerke des denkmalgeschützten Treppenturms des A.K.T; Pforzheim ist Lokshinas gleichnamiger Dokumentarfilm „ Active Vocabulary “ (2025), in dessen Mittelpunkt eine russische Lehrerin steht, die wegen ihrer Kritik am russischen Angriffskrieg gegen die Ukraine denunziert wurde und nach ihrer Flucht nach Deutschland in einem Workshop die Umstände des „Verrats“ aufarbeitet. Über ihr Schicksal setzt sich der Film damit auseinander, wie nach Beginn des russischen Angriffskriegs gegen die Ukraine 2022 russische Schulen zum Instrument staatlicher Propaganda umfunktioniert wurden, um die staatlich kontrollierte Lesart des Krieges und der russisch-ukrainischen Geschichte in den Köpfen der Schüler:innen zu implementieren. Der Dokumentarfilm knüpft dabei, so Esther Buss in ihrer Kritik zum Film, „ein Netz vielfältiger Beziehungen: zwischen imperialer Expansion und innerer Kolonisierung, territorialer und ideologischer Invasion, systemischer Kollaboration und Formen des Widerstandes“.

Dabei geht es Yulia Lokshina nicht nur um die Auseinandersetzung mit den konkreten Zuständen in Russland, sondern um eine Problematik, die uns letztlich alle betrifft: „Im Zeitalter von Digitalisierung und Populismus ist politisch motivierte Manipulation kein isoliertes Phänomen, das nur einzelne Staaten betrifft, sondern von globaler Bedeutung und eine ernstzunehmende Gefahr für die Demokratie“, so Lokshina anlässlich der Ausstellung.

Im Rahmen der Schau , die bis 24. Januar 2027 zu sehen sein wird, wird der Dokumentarfilm erstmals außerhalb von Filmfestivals zu sehen sein; er läuft während der Öffnungszeiten der Ausstellung täglich um jeweils 17 Uhr.

title_original: Le relazioni di Alan Bee da ABC-ARTE Genova
editorial_title_zh: Alan Bee 的“关系”亮相热那亚 ABC-ARTE 画廊
editorial_excerpt_zh: 曾投身当代艺术的商人 Bee带着蜡、蜂蜜和金属网再次来到热那亚。本文原载于 exibart.com。
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "由保罗·坎皮利奥（Paolo Campiglio）策展的《隐秘关系》（Relazioni invisibili）是艾伦·比（Alan Bee）在热那亚 ABC-ARTE 的第二次亮相（第一次展览可在此查看），这位德国金融界人士为了不留遗憾，选择成功地把自己伪装成了一名当代艺术家。因此，这一次全都是关于关系的问题。从他理解绘画的方式中那些典型元素之间的关系开始：六角金属网、蜂蜡与蜂蜜，它们经过恰当的调和，不仅创造了我们所说的“混合媒介”，还创造了艺术家每件作品内部的小宇宙。Bee 的每一件作品本身就是一种关系，它是作品赖以产生的、被赋予功能的各个部分之间全面合作的产物：物理元素被置于一个同样是物理的、真实的、被占用的空间之中。因此，现在是时候关注这个空间了，在这里，我们的存在并非可有可无，正如所有精选作品的存在一样。", "links": [{"text": "qui", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/arte-contemporanea/alan-bee-pitture-abc-arte/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/Alan-Bee-Genesis-1979-mixed-media-on-canvas-30x20x4cm-1-734x1024.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Alan Bee, Genesis, 1979, mixed media on canvas, cm 30x20x4, courtesy ABC-ARTE Genova", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Bee 与作品空间", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "因此，让我们来谈谈空间与作品的关系，反之亦然。对于 Bee 来说，这似乎至关重要，某种程度上就像帕维尔·弗洛连斯基（Pavel Florensky）在《艺术作品中的空间与时间》（Lo spazio e il tempo nell'opera d'arte）中所阐述的那样：无论是 20 世纪 70 年代的《Genesis》，还是 2000 年代的《Freewomen》，以及那些绝对小巧玲珑或实打实的宏大创作（宏大到让你迷失其中，参见《Costa d'Amalfi》），作品都在自我宣告，传达出一种超越其生成手段的在场感。正因如此，作品本身从“对象”的存在转变为“反思对象”的存在。还有一个进一步的转变：Bee 将绘画的二维性视为一种应该抛在脑后的晦涩概念。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/ALANBEE-RELAZIONI-INVISIBILI-curated-by-Paolo-Campiglio-ABC-ARTE-Genoa-Oct.16-Dec.62026sala-piccola-1024x683.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Alan Bee, Relazioni invisibili, installation view, courtesy ABC-ARTE Genova", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "进行三维创作", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Bee 从事三维创作。《隐秘关系》中挑选的作品强调了这一特定方面，从 20 世纪 70 年代自然活体材质的厚重感（蜡面上的那些灼烧痕迹是最地道的欧洲静物画），到 90 年代末和 2000 年代初刺眼的合成色彩过载。为了扮演魔鬼代言人，我们补充说，后者对公众更具吸引力（毫不奇怪，其中一件作品就在我们眼前实时安置妥当），而对那些自诩从事艺术批评的人来说则不然。抛开这些讨好不谈，概念很明确：抛开所属的年代不谈，对 Bee 来说，第三维度绝非偶然。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/Alan-Bee-Free-Force-1999-mixed-media-on-canvas-150x250x4-cm-1024x615.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Alan Bee, Free Force, 1999, mixed media on canvas,, cm 150x250x4, courtesy ABC-ARTE Genova", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "作为在场感的绘画", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Bee 的作品可以从各个角度进行观察（背面除外，这与其说是因为明显的触及限制，不如说是因为 Bee 毕竟仍然留在绘画的领域里）。这并非一条建议，而是一项旨在理解艺术家心目中作品与空间的关系究竟能延伸到何种程度的规定。从这个意义上说，《Resuretio ego sum panis pitie》画框十六厘米的深度之所以重要，与其说是因为它本身，不如说是因为它让我们欣赏到了逆重力而上的色彩流淌，从而超越了将绘画视为纯粹内在效果的观念。因为对 Bee 来说，绘画从来都不是一种抽象的练习，即使当它在 1999 年的《Free Force》中似乎在引用罗伯特·德劳内（Robert Delaunay）的色彩动力学时也是如此。它是真实的在场。", "translated": true}]
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Relazioni invisibili , a cura di Paolo Campiglio , è la seconda uscita genovese di Alan Bee da ABC-ARTE (la prima la trovate qui ), l’uomo di finanza tedesco che per non farsi mancare nulla ha scelto di mascherarsi (con successo) da artista contemporaneo. Stavolta, quindi, è tutta una questione di relazioni. article_text:
Relazioni invisibili , a cura di Paolo Campiglio , è la seconda uscita genovese di Alan Bee da ABC-ARTE (la prima la trovate qui ), l’uomo di finanza tedesco che per non farsi mancare nulla ha scelto di mascherarsi (con successo) da artista contemporaneo. Stavolta, quindi, è tutta una questione di relazioni. A cominciare da quella tra gli elementi tipici del suo modo d’intendere la pittura: la rete metallica a esagoni, la cera e il miele, che armonizzati a dovere non creano solo quella che chiamiamo “tecnica mista”, ma un microcosmo interno a ogni singolo lavoro dell’artista. Ogni opera di Bee è una relazione in sé, frutto di una partnership totale tra parti funzionalizzate da cui ha origine l’opera: elemento fisico inserito in uno spazio altrettanto fisico, reale, occupato. È quindi tempo di concentrarsi su questo spazio, dove la nostra presenza non è accessoria, così come quella di tutti i pezzi selezionati.

Bee e lo spazio dell’opera

Parliamo quindi dello spazio in relazione all’opera e viceversa, che per Bee pare fondamentale un po’ come per Pavel Florensky ne Lo spazio e il tempo nell’opera d’arte : indipendentemente che si tratti degli anni Settanta di Genesis , o dei 2000 di Freewomen , così come di operazioni decisamente pocket o effettivamente monumentali (monumentali nel senso che ti ci perdi dentro, vedere Costa d’Amalfi ), l’opera si auto-dichiara, deliberando un’ammissione di presenza che va oltre i mezzi con cui è stata generata. È così che l’opera stessa si sposta dalla sussistenza di “oggetto” a quella di “oggetto di riflessione”. Con un passaggio ulteriore: Bee tratta la bidimensionalità pittorica come un concetto astruso da lasciarsi alle spalle.

Lavorare in tre dimensioni

Bee lavora in terza dimensione. Le opere scelte per Relazioni invisibili sottolineano questo aspetto specifico, passando dalla corposità di una materia viva naturale (quelle bruciature superficiali su cera sono il più autentico degli still life europei) negli anni ’70, all’overdose di colori sgargiantemente sintetici di fine ’90 primi 2000. Quest’ultimi, aggiungiamo per fare un po’ gli avvocati del diavolo, più ammiccanti per il pubblico (non a caso abbiamo una di queste è stata piazzata in tempo reale sotto i nostri occhi) e meno per chi pretende di occuparsi di critica d’arte. Ammiccamenti a parte, il concetto è chiaro: al netto della decade di appartenenza, la terza dimensione per Bee non è un accidente.

La pittura come presenza

Le opere di Bee si osservano da ogni lato (retro escluso, non tanto per evidenti limiti di accessibilità, quanto perché Bee resta pur sempre nel campo della pittura). E questo non vuole essere un consiglio, ma una prescrizione per capire fin dove la relazione tra opera e spazio può spingersi secondo l’artista. In tal senso, i sedici centimetri di profondità del telaio di Resuretio ego sum panis pitie sono una dimensione che conta non tanto in sé, quanto nel suo farci apprezzare colature di colore che contrastando la gravità superano l’idea di una pittura come puro effetto immanente. Perché la pittura per Bee non è mai un esercizio d’astrazione, anche quando sembra citare il dinamismo cromatico di Robert Delaunay in Free Force del 1999. È presenza reale.

title_original: Il Padiglione Italia alla Biennale di Architettura 2027 sarà curato da (AB)NORMAL + APRIL
editorial_title_zh: 2027年威尼斯建筑双年展意大利馆将由 (AB)NORMAL + APRIL 策展
editorial_excerpt_zh: 文化部长亚历山德罗·朱利在入围的三组方案中，为2027年意大利馆选择了聚焦建筑短暂属性的 TEMPORANEA 项目。斯蒂法诺·博埃里（Stefano Boeri）和保罗·泽尔马尼（Paolo Zermani）的项目也进入了决赛。本文摘自威尼斯双年展意大利馆……

article_text:
Sarà TEMPORANEA , il progetto curatoriale dello studio (AB)NORMAL insieme ad APRIL , a rappresentare l’Italia alla 20. Mostra Internazionale di Architettura della Biennale di Venezia , in programma dall’8 maggio al 21 novembre 2027. La nomina è stata annunciata dal ministro della Cultura Alessandro Giuli , che ha scelto la proposta tra i tre progetti finalisti selezionati attraverso l’avviso pubblico promosso dalla Direzione Generale Creatività Contemporanea del Ministero.

Padiglione Italia 2027: il progetto TEMPORANEA

Al centro di TEMPORANEA c’è la dimensione transitoria dell’architettura, intesa non soltanto come condizione temporale, ma come possibilità di generare esperienze e relazioni. La proposta affronta il tema attraverso un allestimento concepito come una macchina scenica dinamica, capace di restituire la varietà della progettazione italiana e la sua capacità di intervenire in contesti in continuo mutamento. Secondo la commissione di valutazione, il progetto interpreta in modo originale un tema centrale nella pratica architettonica contemporanea, mettendolo in relazione anche con le diverse espressioni del Made in Italy.

« Siamo profondamente grati al Ministro della Cultura Alessandro Giuli, alla Direzione Generale Creatività Contemporanea e ai membri della Commissione per aver creduto nella nostra visione », ha dichiarato lo Studio (AB)NORMAL. « Insieme ad APRIL, con cui condividiamo questo percorso curatoriale, attraverso TEMPORANEA abbiamo l’opportunità di esplorare un’idea di architettura che non si misura nella durata, ma nella sua capacità di generare esperienze, relazioni e immaginari collettivi. Un’occasione per dare voce a una cultura progettuale italiana tanto diffusa quanto ancora poco raccontata » .

Il gruppo curatoriale riunisce due realtà con competenze trasversali tra architettura, ricerca, comunicazione e produzione culturale. (AB)NORMAL è stato fondato dagli architetti Mattia Inselvini , Davide Masserini e Luigi Savio, rispettivamente classi 1992, 1993, 1987; APRIL è composto, invece, da Alessandro Farinella , Monica Moschini e Francesco Maria Tiribelli, nati nel 1975, 1993 e 1971. Le esperienze dei sei professionisti attraversano ambiti differenti, dalla progettazione architettonica alla moda, fino alla curatela di mostre e installazioni.

Visualizza questo post su Instagram Un post condiviso da DG Creatività Contemporanea MiC (@creativita_contemporanea)

Le motivazioni della scelta

La scelta è arrivata al termine di una selezione in due fasi. Oltre a TEMPORANEA , la terna sottoposta al ministro comprendeva Italian Resonances , proposto da Stefano Boeri , e Il nuovo nell’antico. Italia laboratorio d’Europa , di Paolo Zermani . La commissione, presieduta da Costantino D’Orazio e composta da Giovanni Francesco Tuzzolino, Lorenza Baroncelli, Paolo Desideri e Fabio Novembre , ha valutato i progetti in base alla qualità della proposta scientifica, all’originalità e alla fattibilità.

«È un progetto concepito dai giovani per i giovani», ha dichiarato Alessandro Giuli, sottolineando il carattere partecipativo della proposta e la volontà di affidare alle nuove generazioni la possibilità di ripensare gli spazi della vita collettiva. «Affidare il Padiglione Italia della Biennale Architettura 2027 a un gruppo di giovani architetti significa compiere una scelta coraggiosa, una scommessa sul futuro e sulla capacità delle nuove generazioni di interpretare e trasformare il nostro tempo. È un progetto concepito dai giovani per i giovani, fondato su una visione condivisa e partecipativa dell’architettura, che torna a essere terreno privilegiato di sperimentazione. Una proposta radicalmente contemporanea, capace di misurarsi con la dimensione dell’effimero, con linguaggi in continuo divenire, con la distanza tra il tempo ordinario e quello vissuto e percepito dalle nuove generazioni. Uno sguardo inedito sulla realtà, una prospettiva soggettiva che emerge dal magma di interrogativi, inquietudini e aspirazioni che attraversa il nostro presente. Investire sui giovani significa riconoscere il valore delle loro domande, prima ancora delle risposte, e affidare alla loro immaginazione la possibilità di risemantizzare gli spazi, le relazioni e i luoghi della nostra vita collettiva. Credo che per un Ministro della Cultura poche sfide siano più affascinanti di questa: avere il coraggio di guardare avanti, scommettere sul talento emergente e restituire alla sperimentazione la libertà di esplorare territori ancora sconosciuti». Per Massimo Osanna , capo del Dipartimento per le Attività Culturali, il Padiglione offrirà una lettura problematica del contesto architettonico italiano e internazionale, coinvolgendo anche arte contemporanea, design, moda, cinema e spettacolo.

article_text:
The fraught choices and painstaking human labor of film restoration remains a mystery to many viewers, even as new archival releases play an increasingly central role in the life cycle of independent films. Restorationist Ross Lipman’s new essay collection, The Archival Impermanence Project (Sticking Place Books, 2025), aims to pull back the curtain, exploring in detail the decision-making and technical processes behind many of his landmark projects. Along the way, Lipman provides a much-needed meta-analysis of the film-preservation discipline in 2025, outlining a series of questions about the nature of archives, the ephemerality of cultural objects, and the history of cinematic technology.

Lipman was the senior film restorationist at the UCLA Film & Television Archive for 17 years before founding his own restoration and production company, Corpus Fluxus. He has played a crucial role in the rediscovery of American independent classics like The Exiles (Kent Mackenzie, 1961), Wanda (Barbara Loden, 1970), and Killer of Sheep (Charles Burnett, 1978). The Archival Impermanence Project compiles writing from throughout Lipman’s career. Far from a technical manual, however, the book is buoyed throughout by Lipman’s quirky voice, humorous anecdotes, and insider trivia.

The book is broken up into three sections: “Poetics” outlines a theoretical approach to restoration, “Case Studies” describes a series of workflows for individual films Lipman has worked on, and “Histories” includes articles that arose out of the extensive research Lipman conducts as part of the restoration process. Lipman’s key theses are articulated in his 2009 essay “The Gray Zone,” in which he maps a rough “travel guide” to the restoration process. What arises in “the zone” (an allusion to both Ansel Adams and Fred Archer’s system for photographic exposure and Tarkovsky’s dystopian sci-fi Stalker ) are the myriad questions related to a restoration’s supposed authenticity.

These questions are especially pertinent for independent films, where filmmakers rarely retain the level of control over lab procedures that is a given for directors of studio productions. Using a contact printer, lab technicians manipulate qualities like contrast and saturation when striking a new print from a negative—this process is known as “timing” or “grading.” With different cueing methods, it is possible to exercise control over these qualities at the level of individual frames, though it is more common for lighting (and thus contrast and saturation) to vary from shot to shot or scene to scene. But independent productions are rarely allotted the time and money required to regrade an entire project if this process has not been completed to their exact specifications, so as Lipman puts it, “emulating an old release print is preserving the work not of the filmmaker but whoever worked the night shift at Deluxe Labs on a given night in 1975.”

Further complicating notions of authenticity, film archives and museums typically differentiate among archival conservation, preservation, and restoration. Conservation (attentive storage) and preservation (duplication in stable formats) do not fundamentally alter the appearance of a film. Restoration, on the other hand, implies a wholesale reconstruction of a film’s contents, “combining picture and sound elements from different sources in order to restore a work that has been significantly altered back to its original form.”

Viewers might conceive of the restorationist’s task as an objective, scientific endeavor to re-create a film exactly as it originally looked. For Lipman, however, true restoration is a subjective, interpretative art that must be guided by an understanding of the filmmaker’s original vision. In Lipman’s philosophy of film restoration, individual films are actually just abstract aesthetic ideas. When the director makes a film, they give this idea an embodied form as a self-contained work (e.g., an original release print on 35mm). Later, the restorationist helps to realize a new version in an appropriate physical format, drawing from the best surviving elements (e.g., the internegative scanned to 35mm and 4K DCP). In this sense, there is actually no permanently fixed version of any film—just its various iterations in different cuts, print generations, and formats. Because the restorationist inherently maintains a high degree of control over lab procedures like timing, the restored version may ultimately hew closer to the filmmaker’s original intentions than the filmmaker’s original product. As to what all this means for a restoration’s authenticity, the jury is still out.

Thus, in thinking about how to achieve the ideal restoration, Lipman offers a simple-sounding maxim with far-ranging and sometimes contradictory implications: “the final text on any work is the work itself.” Sometimes a living filmmaker can offer helpful consultation throughout the restoration process. More often than not, however, the restorationist must look for obscure clues that indicate how a work was originally meant to look (in inscrutable handwriting on film cans, in the margins of scripts, in diary entries or journals, or within the highlights and shadows of the negative themselves). Strict rules about source elements, aspect ratios, grain, and contrast curves won’t help; just because two films are shot on Eastman Color Negative 5254/7254 100T stock doesn’t mean the contact printer can maintain the same filter settings for timing.

Authenticity is again challenged when Lipman arrives at exhibition, since even two screenings of the same film can be radically different visual and sensory experiences—as anyone who has experienced an unpleasantly long reel break knows all too well. This is a pressing concern amid the “explosion of contexts in which moving images are received.” At one end of the spectrum, viewers now mostly watch movies at home, streamed on personal devices. At the other end, audiences are also more likely than ever to encounter film and video in museums, as traditional art institutions expand their purview to include “time-based media.” The eponymous essay from the book, subtitled “Performing Cinema in the Age of the Death of Everything” (written during the pandemic), relocates a film’s existence in the ephemeral “moment of presentation.”

It is in this context that Lipman deliberates on format, drawing on what art historian Rosalind Krauss terms the “post-medium condition.” For film, Lipman explains, this means “the wholesale de-physicalization of moving images.” The formal instruments of cameras, projectors, and the negatives and prints themselves have historically had outsize influence on films’ content and structure, which were literally ingrained in the medium. This is rapidly changing with the digital decoupling of form and content. Lipman is hardly a purist when it comes to analog formats, emphasizing how digital cleanup tools have their proper place in the restoration process (discussing Cassavetes’s 1968 film Faces , he differentiates between authentic “camera gate hairs,” imprinted on the negative, and distracting “printer gate hairs,” introduced by inattention at the lab). But he still insists that wherever possible, restorations should maintain a film’s original format, seeking out rare stocks or emulating discontinued ones, because “it’s ontologically impossible to replicate one medium in another.” This is not nostalgia for celluloid; it is a phenomenological reality.

Lipman’s impassioned call for nuance—not to prioritize celluloid’s physicality for its own sake, not to label any one restoration as “definitive”—is a welcome counterbalance to the flurry of “new restorations.” The contemporary cinemagoer needs to be able to comprehend and discern what all this archival terminology means. The Archival Impermanence Project is an important contribution to the relatively young genre of books about film restoration, which includes Paul Read and Mark-Paul Meyer’s technical manual Restoration of Motion Picture Film (2000) and Giovanna Fossati’s theoretical monograph From Grain to Pixel (2009). Though the book will appeal most to filmmakers and archival professionals, Lipman’s concerns take on new and broader urgency amid accelerating digitization, which renders the physical properties of light and color as “binary abstractions,” sequences of 1s and 0s—ever more impermanent than plastic celluloid. If films are ideas given physical form, what does it mean for the art of cinema when the entire cycle of production, exhibition, and restoration happens in the digital realm? This fascinating anthology makes clear that it is the process of film restoration, in its constant consideration of authenticity, materiality, and artistic vision, that is uniquely positioned to address the paradox of archival impermanence.
