article_text:
If James Gunn’s Superman was for the classic superhero fans, James Watkins ‘ Clayface is for the horror junkies.

Fittingly penned by Exorcist: Martyrs horror maestro Mike Flanagan and Drive scribe Hossein Amini, Clayface stars Tom Rhys Harries as the titular Batman villain, who starts off as rising actor Matt Hagen from humble Gotham City roots before he crosses the brutal mafioso Szabo (David Dencik).

After Szabo cuts up Matt’s face in one of many graphic scenes, the actor loses his career and just about everything else in his life. But when he discovers the groundbreaking nanotech research of Dr. Caitlyn Corr (Naomi Ackie), he convinces her to restore his face to its former glory, only to result in terrifying side effects and a bloody quest for revenge.

Related Stories

The 65 Movies That Have Made More Than $1 Billion At The Global Box Office

The 5 Best ‘Batman’ Movies Including Christopher Nolan’s ‘The Dark Knight’

Following the upbeat hero’s story of 2025’s Superman , Gunn’s DCU plays with multiple genres in its latest outing, delivering a suspenseful body horror about a bright young star’s transformation into the iconic supervillain from Batman’s rogues’ gallery.

Watch on Deadline

Harries’ undeniable chemistry with Ackie also gives the movie a sexy rom-com element at times, one that evokes Jeff Goldblum and Geena Davis in David Cronenberg’s The Fly (1986), before his charming infatuation grows into something darker and toxic, becoming the monster to her Dr. Frankenstein.

With the discovery of his new abilities, Matt is able to shape-shift into whoever he wants, adding a chilling element reminiscent of John Carpenter’s The Thing (1982) and the 1998 Denzel Washington thriller Fallen . It’s also played for laughs in one scene as Matt gets caught mid-transformation, sporting a little black dress and earrings.

Not only does Watkins nail the jump-scares, but he also spares no detail in the creative kills and graphic body horror scenes, the likes of which you’ll doubtfully see in Man of Tomorrow .

As Matt learns he can regenerate from even the most gruesome injuries, there’s also a Jason X quality to the horror of his super abilities.

The flick is sure to resonate in Hollywood as part of Matt’s journey takes place in the film industry of DC Comics’ L.A. surrogate, Coast City, where a familiar cultural obsession with beauty plays into his arc, as well as his talent for being a thousand different people.

While the movie highlights the reality of corrupt cops who are in the wealthy’s pockets, as well as medical companies that prioritize cosmetic surgery advancements over life-saving discoveries, Clayface never preaches to its audience like previous DCU films might have fallen guilty of doing.

Whether you’re a comic book nerd or a horror junkie, Clayface is worth the price of admission for its genre-driven approach to a lesser-known character, hopefully serving as a roadmap for the DCU’s onscreen future… but maybe brace yourself if you’re squeamish.

article_text:
Universal Pictures said Thursday that the next installment in its The Mummy franchise that will r eturn Brendan Fraser and Rachel Weisz to their starring roles is titled The Mummy: Book of the Dead . The pic remains set to hit theaters on October 15, 2027.

Radio Silence’s Matt Bettinelli-Olpin and Tyler Gillett are directing the new film from a script by The Family Plan ‘s David Coggeshall. The logline remains under wraps.

Related Stories

Brendan Fraser & Rachel Weisz Officially Set For Uni’s Next ‘Mummy’ Movie From Radio Silence; Pic Hits Theaters Early Summer 2028

The 65 Movies That Have Made More Than $1 Billion At The Global Box Office

Fraser and Rachel Weisz return to their roles of Rick and Evie, first played in the 1999 franchise kickoff The Mummy directed by Stephen Sommers. John Hannan, Kevin J. O’Connor and Oded Fehr also return from that original cast for the new installment, joined by Michael Johnston and Numan Acar.

Watch on Deadline

Sean Daniel, who produced The Mummy , 2001’s The Mummy Returns, 2002’s The Scorpion King , The Mummy: Tomb of the Dragon Emperor and 2017’s Tom Cruise-led The Mummy for Universal, returns to produce alongside Project X Entertainment’s William Sherak, James Vanderbilt and Paul Neinstein, and Clayton Townsend. Fraser and Hivemind’s Jason F. Brown are executive producers.

Despite starring in the first two movies, Weisz sat out the third movie, 2008’s The Mummy: Tomb of the Dragon Emperor . Maria Bello took over the role, joining Fraser.

Fraser has since said he’s been waiting 20 years for the call to return to the franchise, which combined has grossed more than $1.8 billion at the global box office.

article_text:
Constantin Film and Sony Pictures’ horror reboot “ Resident Evil ” secured its fourth consecutive weekend at number one across mainland China, grossing RMB28.5 million ($4.3 million) over the Oct. 30–Nov. 1 frame, according to data from Artisan Gateway.

Since launching during the Golden Week corridor on Oct. 5, the video game adaptation has generated a cumulative haul of $71.3 million.

Related Stories

Quentin Tarantino Surprises Fans With 17 Minutes of ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’ at AFI Fest

David Fincher Cut 60 Pages of Tarantino's 'Cliff Booth' Script: 'The First Draft Was 230 Pages. It Was Essentially Two Movies'

New Classics Pictures’ crime procedural drama “ Traces of Justice ” retained second place, bringing in $3.9 million in its fifth weekend. Directed by Chen Sicheng (“Detective Chinatown”) and co-written with Zhang Ji and Yan Zijie, the period investigation epic has pushed its cumulative gross to $98.5 million since rolling out on Oct. 1. Starring Zhang Yi, Ma Li, and Chen Minghao alongside guest appearances by Karry Wang, Fan Chengcheng, and Chen Feiyu, the multi-decade drama tracks an elite public security detective solving complex historical cases based on real events.

Lionsgate’s action thriller “ John Wick ” landed in third position, taking $2.3 million over its three-day opening weekend, 12 years after its 2014 global release. China Film Group, which handled the release, had told original rights buyer Huayi Bros. in 2014 that the film was too violent for China, and regulators rejected it in 2015. Reeves’ work was later pulled from Chinese streaming platforms after he joined a 2022 Tibet House U.S. benefit concert. “John Wick: Chapter 4” and spinoff “Ballerina” reached Chinese cinemas in 2025, but “Chapter 2” and “Chapter 3” have yet to be released there.

Beijing Joy Fun Pictures’ family body-swap comedy “Mr. & Mrs. Pardon” moved to fourth place, taking $2 million over the weekend frame to lift its cumulative gross to $59 million. Directed by Shen Chunyang and written by Ma Duo, the satirical feature stars real-life comedic pair Shen Chunyang and Xiao Shenyang alongside Jia Bing and Yu Yang as a bickering middle-aged couple forced to navigate marriage and domestic friction after swapping bodies.

Dirty Monkeys’ war comedy-drama “Once Upon a Time in the Middle East” rounded out the top five in its twelfth weekend of release, collecting $900,000. Directed by Wen Muye (“Dying to Survive”) and starring Shen Teng, Jiang Qiming, Aarif Rahman, and Omar Sherif, the enduring summer blockbuster has amassed a cumulative total of $356.9 million since launching on Aug. 11.

Mainland China’s overall weekend box office gross slid to $18.2 million, as the market remained locked in a quiet post-holiday fall corridor. The 2026 year-to-date box office reached $4.73 billion, down 29.0% compared to the same period in 2025.
